newsitem.title: UK: EMU could cut Buba profit by nearly $3 bln - report.
newsitem.headline: EMU could cut Buba profit by nearly $3 bln - report.

text.p: The Bundesbank's earnings could be reduced by nearly $3 billion per year while other central banks profit under plans for European economic and Monetary Union (EMU), a report said on Friday.

Central Banking, a quarterly monetary policy journal, carried out research in profits at the European Union's 15 central banks and then analysed what would happen if they were redistributed according to plans for EMU.
"The Bundesbank could lose up to $3 billion a year from EMU and the Bank of England could gain up to $1.6 billion," the journal said.

"Our calculations show that the distribution of central bank profits in the euro area is an issue with major budgetary implications, which has, to date, only been debated by central bankers behind closed doors," the report said.

At the moment, each central bank's profits are transferred to their home government or retained by the banks. But after EMU profits will be parcelled out according to shareholdings in the European Central Bank (ECB), the report said.

The Maastricht Treaty calls for central profits to be divided by shareholdings in the ECB, according to the following formula -- 50 percent for share of EU population and 50 percent for share of EU GDP.
If 1995 profits had been distribued under those arrangements, assuming all 15 countries joined, France, Italy and Britain would gain while Germany and other "hard core" countries would lose.
"It is as if every German citizen promised to pay every French citizen $38 a year for eternity," the report said.

The 15 central banks made profits equivalent to $25.7 billion in 1995, the journal said. The Bundesbank made $8.4 billion, but would have had to give up $2.6 billion under the EMU formula. The Bundesbank has a 22.55 percent shareholding in the European Monetary Institute (EMI), the precursor of the ECB.
